title: CNCF Research Shows Virtual Machines Remain Central as AI Workloads Evolve
partialText: <img src="https://res.infoq.com/news/2026/11/cncf-vm-ai-workloads/en/headerimage/generatedHeaderImage-1794993904528.jpg"/><p>New research from the Cloud Native Computing Foundation (CNCF) and Linux Foundation Research finds that VMs host an average of 53% of production applications, while emerging AI and agentic workloads are creating additional demand for virtualisation, particularly where stronger execution isolation is required.</p> <i>By Craig Risi</i>

title: OpenAI Scales Git for Coding Agents with Pando
partialText: <img src="https://res.infoq.com/news/2026/11/openai-git-pando/en/headerimage/openai-pando-header-1795331180238.jpeg"/><p>OpenAI has detailed Pando, a new backend that scales Git for concurrent coding-agent workloads without replacing familiar Git workflows. The company reports nearly 80% lower median push latency by coordinating branch updates independently and reusing stored packfiles across fetches.</p> <i>By Eran Stiller</i>

title: Presentation: Inferencing for Enterprises
partialText: <img src="https://res.infoq.com/presentations/enterprise-ai-inference-architecture-costs/en/mediumimage/dio-rettori-medium-1793800900455.jpeg"/><p>Dio Rettori discusses the operational realities of enterprise AI inference. Moving beyond fast token generation, he explores why inference requires dedicated systems engineering, tackles GPU utilization pitfalls, compares on-prem versus cloud TCO, and analyzes multi-agent latency determinism. He shares why teams must embed domain ontology directly into models rather than relying solely on RAG.</p> <i>By Dio Rettori</i>

title: Article: Engineering Around Non-Determinism: Evals, Grounding, and Release Gates for AI-Drafted Suspicious Reports
partialText: <img src="https://res.infoq.com/articles/llm-agent-architecture-evals-grounding/en/headerimage/llm-agent-architecture-evals-grounding-header-1795173682566.jpg"/><p>Moving GenAI into high-stakes production requires treating non-determinism as an engineering problem. This architectural blueprint shows engineering leaders and architects how to build trustworthy agentic workflows using knowledge graphs, dual-layer eval judges, CI/CD release gates, and regression testing against golden datasets to automate drafting while maintaining zero-hallucination compliance.</p> <i>By Ritesh Modi, Sasidhar Gudala</i>

title: QCon San Francisco 2026: Lessons from Building a $100M Product in Six Weeks at OpenAI
partialText: <img src="https://res.infoq.com/news/2026/11/qcon-sf-openai-lessons/en/headerimage/generatedHeaderImage-1795453078651.jpg"/><p>At QCon San Francisco 2026, OpenAI's Brian Yang described building the ChatGPT ads product with Codex agents and no human-written code. He outlined layered testing, sandboxes, and batched pull request reviews, and noted failure modes such as code "slop" and unsafe agent actions. He advised gradual adoption and framed engineers as managers of agents.</p> <i>By Daniel Curtis</i>

title: QCon San Francisco 2026: Securing AI Agents in Production
partialText: <img src="https://res.infoq.com/news/2026/11/qcon-ai-agent-security/en/headerimage/header-1795213847070.jpeg"/><p>At QCon San Francisco, Google's Amanda Walker framed AI agents as an insider-risk problem operating at machine speed, and described identity, credential and containment patterns for running them safely in production.</p> <i>By Mark Silvester</i>

title: How LinkedIn Built a View-Agnostic Analytics System for Modern iOS UI Architectures
partialText: <img src="https://res.infoq.com/news/2026/11/linkedin-view-agnostic-analytics/en/headerimage/linkedin-view-agnostic-analytics-1795455502517.jpeg"/><p>To address the challenge posed by modern iOS UI systems where the logical UI structure may not mirror the native UIKit hierarchy, LinkedIn engineers developed a view-agnostic analytics system build around a shared MeasurableNode contract.</p> <i>By Sergio De Simone</i>

title: JEP 545 Moves ZGC Memory Preparation off the Startup Path in JDK 28
partialText: <img src="https://res.infoq.com/news/2026/11/jep-545-jdk-28/en/headerimage/generatedHeaderImage-1795265408975.jpg"/><p>JEP 545, Faster Startup and Warmup with ZGC, has been integrated into JDK 28, moving heap memory preparation onto concurrent worker threads. ZGC now pre-touches memory as it expands and upgrades small pages to large ones on Linux 6.1 and later, but the 2 MB initial heap behind the JEP's 38% startup and 90% warmup gains requires the adaptive heap sizing flag from JEP 546, which is off by default.</p> <i>By A N M Bazlur Rahman</i>

title: Java News Roundup: Java4Shell, Oracle CSPUs, OpenJDK, Azul Payara, BellSoft, Helidon, LangChain4j
partialText: <img src="https://res.infoq.com/news/2026/11/java-news-roundup-nov16-2026/en/headerimage/java-news-roundup-image-1795447387323.jpg"/><p>This week's Java roundup for November 16th, 2026, features news highlighting: the Java4Shell RCE vulnerability; Oracle CSPUs; Lazy Constants targeted for JDK 28; the November 2026 edition of Azul Payara; point releases of Java Operator SDK, LangChain4j and Micrometer; maintenance releases of Liberica JDK and Helidon; and second release candidates of Hibernate Reactive.</p> <i>By Michael Redlich</i>

title: Netflix at QConSF 2026: Retrofitting the SDLC for AI Coding Agents
partialText: <img src="https://res.infoq.com/news/2026/11/netflix-sdlc-ai-coding-agents/en/headerimage/netflix-header-1200x630-1795359626158.jpg"/><p>At QCon San Francisco 2026, Mark Khuzam of Netflix explained how the Commerce team retrofitted its SDLC so AI coding agents and engineers could ship together. The team wrote 45 architecture decision records for people and agents, added a review agent that posts only verified blockers, and serves per-domain GraphRAG context through a single MCP tool.</p> <i>By Andrew Hoblitzell</i>

title: Agoda Reduces API Code Review Time by 64% with Modular Architecture
partialText: <img src="https://res.infoq.com/news/2026/11/agoda-modular-monolith-framework/en/headerimage/generatedHeaderImage-1793569078425.jpg"/><p>Agoda introduced a modular monolith framework in its post-booking API to reduce coupling without a full rewrite. The platform uses domain components, Data Mapper patterns, typed builders, and ArchUnit tests to enforce boundaries. Framework-backed changes showed 64% shorter median code reviews and 34% faster initial feedback than legacy changes.</p> <i>By Leela Kumili</i>

title: Claude Code Adds Experimental Code Mode to Orchestrate Tool Calls with JavaScript
partialText: <img src="https://res.infoq.com/news/2026/11/claude-code-mode/en/headerimage/generatedHeaderImage-1795090945761.jpg"/><p>Anthropic's experimental Code Mode lets Claude Code write JavaScript that chains, parallelizes, and filters Bash, Read, and Edit calls, with changes to how auto mode and hooks review those calls.</p> <i>By Daniel Dominguez</i>

title: Podcast: Simulation Can Tell You What Your Agents are Actually Doing: A Conversation with Zhou Yu
partialText: <img src="https://res.infoq.com/podcasts/simulation-agents-actually-doing/en/smallimage/infoq-podcast-500-1794910149760.jpg"/><p>Michael Stiefel spoke to Zhou Yu about using dynamic simulations to evaluate AI agents. One particular focus was conversational agents where actions depend on prior responses, and the non-deterministic nation of LLMs means you cannot rely on static, reference-based benchmarks. You need to test them using dynamic simulations that incorporate different personas, goals, and corner cases.</p> <i>By Zhou Yu</i>

title: QCon San Francisco 2026: The Harness Is the New Operating System
partialText: <img src="https://res.infoq.com/news/2026/11/harness-new-operating-system/en/headerimage/harness-header-1200x630-1795301479582.jpg"/><p>At QCon San Francisco 2026, Mad Labs founder and CEO Manju Rajashekhar opened the conference arguing that the harness around an AI model, rather than the model itself, decides what an agent can do and how safely it does it. The keynote mapped the parts of a harness, including context, tools, state, permissions and feedback loops, onto jobs that operating systems already perform.</p> <i>By Andrew Hoblitzell</i>

title: PostgreSQL 19 Released with Online Table Repacking and Query Planning Controls
partialText: <img src="https://res.infoq.com/news/2026/11/postgresql-19-released/en/headerimage/generatedHeaderImage-1795349035334.jpg"/><p>The PostgreSQL Global Development Group released PostgreSQL 19, introducing changes to database maintenance, query planning, replication, and application development. The release focuses on reducing administrative overhead and improving performance, with new tools for reorganizing tables without downtime and controlling query plans.</p> <i>By Robert Krzaczyński</i>
